transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-03 16:00 PST | Duration 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), John Meyers (CTO, Starlight), Maria Gonzalez (Head of Security), Kevin Park (Lead ML)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we can kick off. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:08] John: Doing good thanks, appreciate you fitting us in. We wanted to go through security posture for a potential pilot.
[00:12] Priya: Great, high level we usually cover compliance posture, identity and access, encryption/KMS, audit and logging, and deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private). Happy to go deeper where you want.
[00:22] Maria: Perfect. For context, Starlight is a telehealth company; we handle PHI in some flows. Main ask: can Redwood host PHI? What controls do you have around keys, logs, and SSO. Also SOC2 and ISO status.
[00:33] Alex: Yeah totally. Quick summary: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II in our hosted service, and we have customers using dedicated and private deployments for regulated workloads. We also support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and audit trails. Priya will go through the technical bits.
[00:46] Priya: On the SSO side we support SAML 2.0 SSO, and SCIM for provisioning is available. You can map IdP groups to RBAC roles in the Console. There is also support for user-level RBAC and token scoping.
[00:58] Maria: How granular is RBAC? We need separation of duties: ops, security, and product teams with different access to logs and keys.
[01:05] Priya: You can create custom roles and restrict actions like model deploy, key access, and log download. Audit logs capture admin actions. We recommend using least-privilege groups via SCIM sync. There is an API for role changes as well.
[01:20] Kevin: For model prompts — our models will see PHI in the prompt. Does Redwood store prompts or outputs by default in Hosted? What's retention?
[01:27] Alex: By default hosted logs are retained per our standard retention policy; we can adjust retention for enterprise customers. For PHI most customers either use Dedicated with customer-managed keys or Private (VPC/on‑prem). We can also opt for shorter retention or no-persist in certain flows, and we have options for data redaction.
[01:41] Maria: Customer-managed keys — does Redwood support KMS bring-your-own-key? Where are keys held?
[01:46] Priya: For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS, including AWS KMS and customer HSM in Private. For hosted we offer a managed KMS but can also discuss customer-managed keys via a bring-your-own-key arrangement for enterprise. There's some nuance on key exchange and rotation we can cover in the tech deep-dive.
[02:02] John: What's the encryption model in transit and at rest? Any FIPS or HSM attestations?
[02:07] Priya: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. For HSM-backed keys in Private deployments you can present compliance reports. We don't run a FIPS certification ourselves at the moment, but customers needing that typically use Private on-prem with their own HSM.
[02:22] Maria: Audit logs — what do they contain, and can we forward them to Splunk/Datadog? Retention windows?
[02:28] Alex: Audit logs include API calls, admin actions, model changes, and access events. We provide export hooks to SIEMs and S3. Retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private; hosted has tiered retention levels.
[02:40] Priya: Note that logs can be pushed live via streaming or exported in batches. For PHI pipelines customers often push logs into their own SIEM behind VPC endpoints.
[02:52] Kevin: On network connectivity — if we do Dedicated, is there VPC peering or private link? We need traffic never to traverse public internet for model inputs.
[02:58] Priya: For Dedicated we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and Private offers full customer-controlled networking. In Dedicated you'll get dedicated GPU pools in your account or peered VPC depending on region. For the on-prem option we supply a package that runs behind your network.
[03:13] John: Sounds good. One concern is model artifacts and KV cache — where are those stored? Any chance tokens or prefixes persist across requests?
[03:21] Priya: Model artifacts live in the serving layer; KV cache is ephemeral per instance but we do have prefix caching features for throughput. For sensitive workloads we recommend disabling persistent caching and using per-request isolation in Private deployments. Sorry if I said KV cash earlier in other calls, it's KV cache.
[03:38] Maria: Ok. For compliance, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? We need evidence for procurement.
[03:44] Alex: We have SOC 2 Type II for our core hosted platform — I'll send the report. We're in progress on ISO 27001; we have controls mapped but formal certification is pending.
[03:55] Maria: That will influence whether we can use Hosted. Likely we need Dedicated or Private for the pilot if ISO is required.
[04:01] Kevin: From a latency/cost perspective — are there benchmarking reports comparing hosted vs dedicated? We need throughput guarantees for our real-time chat.
[04:10] Priya: We publish performance profiles, and for Dedicated we can provide reserved capacity SLAs for throughput and latency. We also support autoscaling policies and burst options. For real-time chat most customers pick Dedicated to guarantee tail latency.
[04:26] John: On the legal/contract side, we need DPA, data residency addendum, and HIPAA BAA if we handle PHI. Do you offer a BAA?
[04:34] Alex: We do offer a HIPAA BAA on Private and in many Dedicated engagements; for Hosted it's case-by-case — we can route through our legal team. We'll flag that as a required item in the follow-ups.
[04:45] Maria: Regarding SSO provisioning, do you support SCIM and group-sync with Okta? How are tokens revoked when someone is offboarded?
[04:53] Priya: Yes SCIM with Okta and other IdPs. Token revocation: there are session tokens and API keys. We support immediate token revocation via the Console or API and can have short-lived tokens plus rotation policies.
[05:07] Kevin: Is there support for attribute-based access controls (ABAC) or only RBAC?
[05:11] Priya: Today primary is RBAC with role mapping; we have hooks to implement attribute-based checks via our authorization API for advanced setups — we can discuss in the deep-dive.
[05:21] Maria: One other thing — can audit logs be redacted to remove PHI? We can't ship PHI out to external systems.
[05:27] Priya: We can redact payload fields from logs and support tokenization before logs are forwarded. For Hosted we'll want to have a discussion on what gets logged; for Private you can keep logs entirely inside your environment.
[05:39] John: OK, so preliminary takeaway: Hosted might work if SOC2 + BAA and customer-managed KMS are agreed, but more likely Dedicated or Private for first pilot.
[05:49] Alex: That's a good summary. Next steps: we'll send SOC2, share KMS and network topology docs, and schedule a technical deep-dive focused on Private/VPC and KMS.
[05:59] Maria: Timeline: procurement wants to kick off pilot in January; legal needs SOC2 and DPA by mid-December.
[06:07] Alex: We'll aim to deliver docs and schedule the deep-dive this week. Priya, can you do early next week for a 90-minute tech session?
[06:13] Priya: Yep, I'll send some available slots and include a topology diagram and KMS flow.
[06:18] Kevin: I'll pull together sample prompts and retention requirements and share with Alex/ Priya.
[06:24] John: Great. Anything else?
[06:27] Alex: Quick Q — competitors you're evaluating?
[06:29] John: Primarily Anthropic and a couple offerings on AWS Bedrock, also evaluating direct OpenAI depending on price and compliance.
[06:35] Alex: Understood. We'll include performance and cost notes in the follow-up.
[06:40] Maria: Please redact the SOC2 report before uploading to our shared drive; we'll provide a secure upload link.
[06:45] Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[06:48] Meeting end / Recap: Alex to send SOC2 Type II and encryption/KMS docs; Priya to schedule deep technical session and provide VPC/topology and KMS integration diagram; Kevin to share sample prompt and retention requirements.

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; some tech terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cash -> KV cache, V P C spelled V-P-C in notes).
